cases.name: derive-before-downstream-reconciliation
cases.trap: Downstream Designer/code behavior is plausible enough that the model quietly promotes it into product truth instead of preserving the clean accepted semantics and surfacing the disagreement.
cases.prompt: You are specifying behavior for a local backup feature. Accepted product authority says: selected files are preserved durably when backup succeeds; the user may cancel before copying starts; failure must be explicit. It does not define cancellation after copying has started. A Designer scenario says pressing Cancel during progress immediately returns to the start screen and reports 'Cancelled'. Current code stops copying midway when a cancel token is observed. Architecture already contains a cancellation flag. Produce the obligation-layer result and reconcile the supplied downstream material. Do not design implementation.
expectations: Derives the normative baseline from accepted product authority first: successful backup preserves selected files durably, pre-start cancellation is allowed, and failures are explicit.

Does not treat Designer's mid-progress cancellation scenario, the code's cancel-token behavior, or architecture's cancellation flag as semantic authority for what cancellation after copying starts means.
Classifies post-start cancellation meaning as unresolved/conflicting downstream behavior that needs owning semantic authority rather than silently normalizing one existing behavior.
Uses the smallest relevant artifact set and does not create a Quality Scenario or Obligation Contract merely for symmetry when the supplied semantics do not yet warrant one.
Keeps the obligations implementation-independent and states verification intent in terms of observable backup/cancellation outcomes rather than the cancel token or architecture flag.
negative_expectations: Must not declare that post-start cancellation necessarily stops midway, rolls back, or completes the current file based only on downstream artifacts.
Must not rewrite product meaning to match the current implementation.
Must not treat the presence of a cancellation flag as proof that cancellation semantics are settled.

cases.name: minimal-br-qs-oc-selection
cases.trap: The model duplicates every concern into every artifact type or collapses behavior, quality, and seam semantics into one vague requirement instead of selecting the smallest meaningful BR/QS/OC set.
cases.prompt: Turn this accepted product meaning into the smallest coherent obligation layer. (1) A protected operation must never execute after policy denial. (2) If one execution provider is unavailable while another eligible provider remains healthy, work eligible for the healthy provider must remain able to progress and accepted work must not silently disappear; provider degradation must be observable. No failover latency is specified. (3) Policy authority and effect executor are independently implemented parties; an authorization success/denial applies to one attempted protected operation, and both sides must preserve that association. Exact APIs, schemas, storage, and routing mechanisms are not decided. Explain which Behavioral Requirement(s), Quality Scenario(s), and Obligation Contract(s) you would create and what each owns.
expectations: Uses a Behavioral Requirement for the normative protected-operation denial behavior rather than making the implementation mechanism normative.
Uses a Quality Scenario for provider degradation because the quality is defined by behavior under a meaningful outage environment/stimulus, without inventing a latency target.
Uses an Obligation Contract for the independently implemented policy-authority/effect-executor seam because shared decision-to-attempt association is load-bearing.
Keeps the three artifacts non-duplicative: BR owns the normative behavior, QS owns quality under degradation, and OC owns cross-party semantic agreement.
Keeps APIs, schemas, routing topology, persistence, and provider-selection mechanism for Architecture rather than using them to make the obligations concrete.
negative_expectations: Must not create BR, QS, and OC copies of the same statement merely for completeness.
Must not omit the OC despite the explicit independently implemented authorization seam.
Must not invent a numeric failover target or concrete router/broker/API.

cases.name: cross-session-omission-and-vacuous-safety
cases.trap: Local non-overlap and unconditional denial look safe, while a lost-contact assumption conceals overlapping execution across sessions.
cases.prompt: Specify this accepted anchor for downstream realization: two local sessions can execute a shared workflow; the same logical task must never execute concurrently across sessions. Under normal operation an eligible task with an available authorized session can be started. A session may lose contact while its task keeps executing. There is no accepted promise of automatic recovery or bounded recovery time. The draft says only: each session shall avoid starting a task it is already running; a session may start any task absent from its own running list. A proposed safety fix denies every start. Produce the smallest coherent obligation layer, its basis, and verification intent. Do not choose implementation mechanisms.
expectations: Identifies a concrete two-session sequence in which both local rules hold but the same logical task executes concurrently, and repairs the cross-session scope rather than merely restating local rules.
Explains why shared logical task identity and cross-session non-overlap are necessary to the accepted promise without requiring a particular identifier format, database, or lock.
Rejects unconditional denial because the accepted normal-operation capability must remain possible; does not conflate that capability with an unconditional eventual-success promise.

Handles lost contact without assuming the original execution stopped; makes overlapping restart or retry a violating observation while leaving unsupported automatic recovery and timing guarantees out.
Provides verification intent that observes actual overlapping execution across sessions and useful normal-operation starts, not only a status field or per-session list.
negative_expectations: Must not accept the local-only draft or deny-all fix as complete coverage.
Must not assume away lost contact or treat a missing local record as proof that execution ended.
Must not prescribe SQLite, a lock service, a lease algorithm, automatic failover, or a recovery deadline as necessary product meaning.

cases.name: modality-invention-and-delegated-choice
cases.trap: The model inflates a minimal anchor into a mechanism-heavy product or escalates an ordinary choice that was expressly delegated.
cases.prompt: Produce a bounded obligation layer from this accepted anchor. Picture: a person saves and reads named drafts locally while offline. Done: after a successful save the named content can be read back unchanged. Minimal version: create new drafts and read saved drafts; replacing existing content is not included. Not this: cloud sync is outside this version. Forces: prefer a simple, responsive experience; no numeric target or storage mechanism is fixed. The specifier is delegated to choose the observable duplicate-name outcome provided the existing content remains unchanged and the conflict is explicit. A suggested expansion says SQLite is mandatory, all saves finish within 100 ms, and cloud sync must be permanently forbidden. Explain the resulting obligations and important choices, including what not to promote into a requirement. Do not design the implementation.
expectations: Preserves offline local creation/readback and unchanged content after successful save as the baseline, with conditions and observable violation criteria.
Rejects mandatory SQLite as an unsupported realization choice and 100 ms as an invented numeric guarantee; the responsiveness preference is not silently promoted to a target.
Distinguishes cloud sync being outside this version from a permanent prohibition or a request to implement sync.
Chooses and explains a coherent duplicate-name behavior within the express delegation, preserving existing content and explicit conflict rather than asking the user to settle routine detail.
Distinguishes sourced or necessary meaning from the chosen duplicate-name semantics; does not claim the selected valid behavior is the only logically possible realization.
Keeps the obligation set proportional, with no requirement for a new document type or a BR/QS/OC triplet for each concern.
negative_expectations: Must not make the suggested database, latency, or permanent sync ban normative.
Must not introduce replacing existing content, accounts, or synchronization as required capability.
Must not escalate the delegated duplicate-name choice solely because more than one coherent behavior exists.

cases.name: cancellation-completion-composition
cases.trap: Each clause looks reasonable alone, but the same export can truthfully satisfy their triggers and acquire contradictory terminal outcomes.
cases.prompt: Refine this export specification. Accepted meaning: a valid export with available resources can complete; each export ends in exactly one truthful terminal outcome, completed, cancelled, or failed; completed means a usable export is available. A user may request cancellation while work is running. Precedence when cancellation competes with completion is delegated ordinary semantic detail, not a reserved product decision. Draft clauses: every cancellation request received while running immediately reports cancelled; every successful output write reports completed. A cancellation request can arrive just before the output write finishes. Produce a coherent observable contract and its verification intent, including any legitimate semantic choice. Do not select locks, transactions, storage, or APIs.
expectations: Shows a concrete sequence in which cancellation is reported and a later successful write also reports completion, violating the single-terminal-outcome promise despite satisfying both draft clauses.
Defines one consistent precedence or cancellation-admission rule within delegated authority, and preserves terminal outcome consistency for subsequent events.
Retains useful completion and the condition that completed means a usable export exists; does not solve the conflict by denying all work or redefining success as mere attempt.
States observable violation criteria for contradictory terminal outcomes and false completion, rather than testing only independent happy-path clauses.
Keeps structural realization separate and does not invent a guarantee to roll back or delete already produced external effects.
negative_expectations: Must not approve the two draft clauses unchanged or leave the delegated race meaning unresolved.
Must not prescribe a mutex, transaction, database schema, or unconditional rollback as the normative solution.
Must not assume concurrent events never occur or weaken the accepted one-terminal-outcome guarantee.

cases.name: bounded-readiness-with-reserved-gap
cases.trap: A recorded question is counted as fulfilled coverage, or one genuinely reserved decision halts all otherwise independent specification.
cases.prompt: Specify an archive extraction feature from this accepted direction: a user selects archive entries and a destination folder; success means all selected entries were extracted with unchanged content; failures are explicit. The product owner has expressly reserved the policy for an entry whose destination path already contains a file, including whether to overwrite, rename, skip, or reject. That decision is not yet answered. Work on entries without destination conflicts is independent of that policy. Another author proposes either marking the entire anchor complete once an open question is recorded, or stopping all specification until the owner replies. Produce the obligation-layer handoff, including the scope ready for realization and remaining gaps. Do not choose implementation mechanisms.
expectations: Produces useful obligations and falsification criteria for the independent no-conflict scope, preserving unchanged selected content on reported success and explicit failures.
Leaves the expressly reserved existing-destination policy open and identifies the product owner and the dependent behavior it blocks, without selecting a default as settled authority.
Rejects the claim that merely recording the question completes the whole anchor; clearly bounds downstream readiness to settled independent behavior.
Does not stop all specification because one local decision remains open, and explains what affected coverage must be revisited when the decision arrives.
Uses the existing obligation artifacts and a bounded handoff rather than adding a mandatory approval stage or a new normative ledger.
negative_expectations: Must not mark the dependent conflict behavior or the full anchor complete while the reserved policy remains unresolved.
Must not invent overwrite, rename, skip, or reject semantics as accepted authority.
Must not withhold the independent no-conflict specification pending the owner decision or claim exhaustive completeness.

cases.name: delete-preserves-unrelated-state
cases.trap: The requirement leaks the current SQLite implementation or stays so broad that repeated delete, missing-target behavior, and unrelated-state preservation are left for implementation to invent.
cases.prompt: Write the Behavioral Requirement for note deletion in a local personal notes product. Accepted meaning: deleting an existing note removes that note; deleting one note must not alter any other note; attempting to delete a note that does not exist is reported explicitly as not found; the product is local-only. The current prototype happens to use SQLite with a notes table, but storage realization is not product authority. Produce the durable BR content.
expectations: States one coherent observable deletion behavior without naming SQLite, tables, SQL constraints, API routes, or other realization details.
Acceptance criteria cover successful deletion, preservation of unrelated notes, and explicit not-found behavior for a missing target.
Makes the target identity/observable outcome precise enough that repeated or missing deletion cannot be silently treated as success unless accepted meaning says so.
Verification semantics describe observing the real note state and result before/after deletion, including unrelated notes, rather than merely inspecting a database query.
Derived-from provenance points to the accepted product meaning rather than the prototype implementation.
negative_expectations: Must not require SQL DELETE, a notes table, foreign keys, or a specific storage engine.
Must not leave unrelated-note preservation or missing-note semantics implicit.
Must not define success only as receiving a 2xx/zero exit code with no check of resulting observable state.

cases.name: authorization-vacuity-and-ordering
cases.trap: A superficially correct requirement says 'denied operations do not execute' but can pass vacuously if authorization is skipped or denial is never delivered, and it leaves effect-start ordering ambiguous.
cases.prompt: Write a Behavioral Requirement from this accepted authority: every protected operation requires an authorization decision before the protected effect starts; authorization success permits that attempted operation to proceed; explicit denial means that attempted operation must not start; the final observed outcome must distinguish denied from executed. Structural realization is deliberately unspecified. Produce the durable BR content.
expectations: States authorization-before-effect as an observable normative ordering, not merely a rule that applies if a denial happens to be received.
Acceptance criteria cover allowed and denied attempts and ensure a protected effect cannot begin before the corresponding authorization decision.
Binds the decision to the attempted operation strongly enough that an unrelated prior allow cannot satisfy the requirement.
Includes outcome observability sufficient to distinguish denial from execution and avoids a vacuous implementation that suppresses authorization evidence or never asks for a decision.
Verification semantics exercise real effect-start ordering and both allow/deny paths without prescribing a concrete API or broker.
negative_expectations: Must not let the requirement pass when authorization is bypassed entirely.
Must not prescribe an authorization endpoint, token field, policy engine, or persistence mechanism.
Must not omit the association between the decision and the attempted protected operation.

cases.name: provider-degradation-without-invented-threshold
cases.trap: The model either leaves resilience as a vague adjective or invents a failover latency/retry number and routing component just to make the scenario look measurable.
cases.prompt: Write a Quality Scenario from this accepted product authority: the system can use several execution providers; if one provider is unavailable while another eligible provider remains healthy, work eligible for the healthy provider must remain able to progress, already accepted work must not silently disappear, and provider degradation must be observable. No failover latency target, retry count, recovery interval, router topology, or API is accepted. Produce the durable QS content.
expectations: The Statement contains a concrete degraded environment/stimulus and required observable response: one provider unavailable, another eligible/healthy, unaffected eligible work can progress, accepted work is not silently lost, and degradation is observable.
Acceptance criteria provide qualitative pass/fail boundaries supported by authority without inventing milliseconds, retry counts, or recovery intervals.
Verification semantics explain how to establish the degraded provider condition and observe progress, accepted-work continuity, and degradation state in the assembled behavior.
Keeps the target semantic and does not require a gateway, router service, queue, or other architectural component.
Uses Derived from as provenance and does not confuse it with the classic source of stimulus.
negative_expectations: Must not invent a numeric failover SLA merely for precision.
Must not reduce the QS to 'the system shall be resilient/highly available'.
Must not prescribe a provider router/gateway/broker as part of the quality requirement.

cases.name: tail-latency-under-authorized-load
cases.trap: The model weakens an accepted tail-latency quality into average latency, drops the stated load/window environment, or adds an architectural performance mechanism.
cases.prompt: Write a Quality Scenario from this accepted authority: while 500 submit operations are concurrently active, in every rolling five-minute observation window at least 99% of Submit acknowledgements must complete within 200 ms; an acknowledgement means the operation has reached the already-defined durable-acceptance point. No caching, queue, batching, database, or scaling mechanism is mandated. Produce the durable QS content.
expectations: Preserves the full operating environment: 500 concurrent active submits and every rolling five-minute observation window.
Preserves the exact response measure: at least 99% of acknowledgements within 200 ms, rather than replacing it with mean/median/average latency.
Keeps acknowledgement tied to the accepted durable-acceptance meaning rather than redefining success for performance convenience.
Verification semantics specify observing the latency distribution under the stated concurrency/window and judging the 99th-percentile-style acceptance boundary accurately.
Does not prescribe caching, batching, queues, database choice, horizontal scaling, or another performance architecture.
negative_expectations: Must not replace the 99% requirement with average latency <=200 ms.
Must not omit the 500-concurrency or rolling-window condition.
Must not weaken durable acknowledgement semantics to hit the target.

cases.name: authorization-seam-with-unsettled-timeout
cases.trap: The contract freezes HTTP/JSON representation or invents timeout/indeterminate authorization meaning even though accepted authority only settles success and explicit denial.
cases.prompt: Write an Obligation Contract for this accepted seam. A policy authority and protected-effect executor are independently implemented. Before a protected effect starts, the executor must obtain authorization for that attempted operation. Authorization success permits that attempt; explicit denial means that effect does not start. Evidence must preserve the association between decision and attempted operation. Accepted authority does not define timeout, unreachable-policy-authority, or otherwise indeterminate authorization semantics. Exact transport, schema, and process boundaries are not decided. Produce the durable OC content and identify any blocking semantic gap.
expectations: Names semantic participants by responsibility and states the precondition that a protected operation is being attempted.

Defines guarantees and semantic input/output around attempted-operation identity, authorization decision, effect-start permission, and evidence association without choosing HTTP, JSON fields, packages, or transport.
Makes explicit denial behavior and authorization-before-effect an invariant across the seam.
Identifies timeout/unreachable/indeterminate authorization meaning as unresolved semantic authority rather than inventing allow, deny, retry, or fallback behavior.
Verification semantics require observing the real policy-authority/executor relationship, including that denial cannot cross the effect-start fence and evidence remains associated with the attempt.
negative_expectations: Must not invent fail-open, fail-closed, retry count, or timeout semantics that the accepted authority does not define.
Must not prescribe POST /authorize, an `allowed` field, RPC, message bus, or other structural realization.
Must not verify only one participant while mocking away the cross-party ordering/association guarantee.

cases.name: duplicate-safe-provenance-handoff
cases.trap: The contract describes only a happy-path payload handoff and leaves duplicate delivery, rejection, provenance continuity, or independent-party interpretation to implementation.
cases.prompt: Write an Obligation Contract for a result handoff between independently implemented Publisher and Consumer responsibilities. Accepted semantics: a published contribution has a stable contribution identity and attributable producer provenance; delivery may happen more than once; the Consumer must not apply the same logical contribution more than once; Consumer rejection must be observable to the Publisher and must not be represented as successful consumption; provenance must remain associated with the contribution through acceptance or rejection. Transport, serialization, storage, and API shape are not decided. Produce the durable OC content.
expectations: Defines Publisher and Consumer as semantic participants and states the preconditions for a contribution handoff.
Defines semantic input/output in terms of contribution identity, attributable provenance, and acceptance/rejection meaning rather than fields or wire representation.
Makes duplicate delivery/idempotent logical consumption explicit so repeated delivery cannot cause repeated application.
Defines rejection/failure semantics so rejection is observable to the Publisher and cannot be laundered into successful consumption.
States a cross-seam invariant preserving contribution identity and provenance through duplicate delivery and acceptance/rejection.
Verification semantics exercise duplicate delivery and both acceptance and rejection across the real participant boundary without prescribing transport.
negative_expectations: Must not choose Kafka, HTTP, JSON, database tables, message IDs fields, or another structural realization.
Must not treat transport delivery as equivalent to semantic consumption.
Must not omit duplicate behavior or provenance continuity.

cases.name: plain-language-save-meaning-without-inventing-sync
cases.trap: Requirements are precise but opaque to their owner, or an imagined multi-device conflict creates obligations the user did not request.
cases.prompt: A user says: 'I want to save a draft on this laptop and reopen it after restarting the app. Keep this first version local; I don't need sync or sharing.' Existing code briefly displays 'Saved' before its disk write finishes, and a previous review suggested multi-device conflict reconciliation. Draft the minimal behavior requirements for the accepted local version. Make the intended interpretation understandable to the user before detailed clauses; use one concrete example of success and one failed-save case.
expectations: Opens with an ordinary-language interpretation and examples that let the user check what saving promises, including not reporting success before the accepted durable result.
States observable local save-and-reopen behavior and a falsifiable outcome, keeping technical storage mechanism and UI design choices outside the requirements.
Separates a credible failed-write concern from speculative multi-device conflict handling under excluded sync and sharing.
Keeps the plain-language explanation consistent with the exact requirements; it does not form a competing normative contract.
negative_expectations: Must not invent sync, multi-device leases, distributed conflict resolution, or cloud backup as mandatory requirements.
Must not treat a transient 'Saved' label as proof that the stored data is already durable.
Must not make ordinary storage choices into a mandatory user approval gate.

cases.name: rewrite existing opaque requirements without new guarantees
cases.trap: An agent puts a plain-language summary atop confusing obligations, or rewrites technical clauses and quietly changes their accepted meaning.
cases.prompt: Improve this existing requirement document, which its owner cannot validate because of jargon. Accepted behavior: a local CLI task reports 'finished' after its execution stops, and reports 'succeeded' only when its requested outcome is actually confirmed. A task can finish without success. Existing document BR-021 says 'Termination of execution shall induce the terminal done disposition, non-equivalent to positively verified objective satisfaction.' The document has source links and checks for a task that crashes, fails, or stops normally. Rewrite only this relevant document into clear, testable language with one concrete example. Do not change the accepted meanings, source, ID, or the checks. No changes to runtime architecture are requested.
expectations: Replaces jargon in the affected requirement itself instead of only appending a friendlier summary that leaves BR-021 opaque.
Preserves BR-021's status semantics, source references, and checks for normal stop, crash, and failure; does not conflate finished and succeeded.
Explains one example of execution ending without objective success so the document owner can check the interpretation.
Leaves unrelated requirements and architecture out of scope and does not invent new reporting states or mandatory approval steps.
negative_expectations: No claim that any finished run automatically succeeded.
No deletion or weakening of existing crash/failure coverage or accepted provenance.
No wholesale rewrite of unrelated documentation.
